reason: Connecting the motor neuron to the muscle junction seems like a useful first step toward controlling the arm.
expectation: I expect a motor connection that can eventually link the spinal cord to a muscle.

alternatives.reason: The stretch-sensing pathway also supports the goal, but I chose to start with movement.

effect: The motor pathway explains how a nerve signal can trigger the calcium release involved in contraction. I will now build a sensory connection.
reaction: The link back to the earlier calcium signal is satisfying.
reason: The sensory neuron ending surrounds the muscle spindle, so combining them should establish a stretch-sensing pathway.
expectation: I expect a connection that carries information about muscle stretch toward the nervous system.

alternatives.reason: Adding touch-sensitive skin also supports the goal, but I want to finish the muscle-related pathway first.

effect: The spindle and sensory neuron form a stretch pathway leading toward the spinal cord. I will add the touch-sensitive skin next.
reaction: The result matches my expectation, though it adds little explanation.
reason: Adding skin with touch receptors to the arm is the only offered combination and should prepare the touch pathway.
expectation: I expect an arm with touch-sensitive skin that can connect to the sensory fibres.

effect: The arm now has marked slots for motor, stretch and touch pathways. I can attach the pathways already made.
reaction: The slots make the next steps clear.
reason: I will attach the motor pathway to connect the muscle control route to the arm.
expectation: I expect the motor slot to be filled, leaving the sensory connections to add.

alternatives.reason: The stretch pathway is also ready, but I chose to attach the motor pathway first.

effect: The motor pathway filled its slot; the stretch and touch connections remain.
reason: The stretch pathway is ready, so I will attach it to the arm.
expectation: I expect the stretch slot to be filled, leaving the touch connection.

alternatives.reason: The touch fibres also fit, but I chose to attach the completed stretch pathway first.

effect: The stretch pathway is fitted, leaving the touch connection to add.
reason: The touch fibres are the only offered combination and should complete the arm's pathway slots.
expectation: I expect the touch slot to be filled, leaving the arm ready to connect to the brain and spinal cord.

effect: The touch fibres filled the last slot, and the explanation distinguishes touch from muscle stretch as sources of sensory information. The arm is ready to connect to the brain and spinal cord.
reaction: The distinction between skin deformation and stretch sensing makes the two sensory pathways clearer.
reason: Connecting the completed arm pathways to the brain and spinal cord is the only offered combination and directly serves the goal.
expectation: I expect a responsive arm connected to the nervous system, completing the goal.

effect: The completed arm connects incoming sensory signals and outgoing motor commands, showing how feedback can help adjust movement.
reaction: The final connection ties the pathways together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the arm to the brain and spinal cord was most worthwhile because it brought the sensory and motor pathways together and explained their roles in movement.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the prepared pathways into slots was straightforward but repetitive; the individual fittings added little explanation.

surprise.text: The distinction between skin deformation and muscle stretch clarified how the two sensory pathways provide different information.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the order of fitting the available pathways seemed interchangeable.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter to see how the responsive arm connects to the rest of the body, though I would hope for more explanatory results between fittings.
